decisionsTitle: «Vii mâine la …?»: the day before a ticked run, the newsletter's subscribers are asked by email, and one tap answers (amending §445, §775 and §812)
decisionsSection:
**The owner, 2026-10-18 01:00–01:20**, building on «Vin!» (§812): «I need this "Going" to be via email or something … super easy». §812 gave the event's page, the token page and the count; this adds the channel where nobody has to open the site: the club's newsletter asks, and one tap answers.

**Decision.** The day before an event the club ticked «Vin!» on, the confirmed newsletter subscribers who chose the topic **«Întrebarea «Vii?» înaintea alergărilor»** (`RSVP_ASK`) — or «Toate noutățile», when that was chosen under a notice that names the question — get ONE email, «Vii mâine la <eveniment>?», with the event's facts block (§392), the event's calendar file, the newsletter's own way out, and two buttons: **«Vin»** counts them at once, **«Nu vin»** counts nobody. It builds on §812 and changes none of its rules: an answer is still not a registration (no place, no declaration, no participant; the allocator, the registrations and the capacity formula never meet it), the gate is still `rsvpOffered` (so the privacy notice in force must name `{{rsvp}}` in both languages), a name is still public only by the person's own tick. **And it has a switch of its own: `{{rsvpAsk}}`** (below).

**A topic of its own, not «Alergările săptămânale» (amends §445).** The new-event alert's topic for a group run says in its hint «o dată pe serie, nu la fiecare alergare» — a subscriber who chose it was promised one message per series — so a question before every run would break what they were told. `RSVP_ASK` is added to the `newsletter_topic` enum (migration 0170, expand only; the value is appended last), offered in the pop-up and on the subscriber's own page like the others, and **off until ticked** (a subscription to everything receives it too, but only if its consent was given under a notice that names the question: next paragraph). It is an `AUTOMATIC_TOPICS` member: no organizer composes a newsletter under it (the composer, `SENDABLE_TOPICS` and the per-topic counts leave it out), because what the subscriber chose is a question with two answers. Its label keeps its inner quotes as «…» (`Întrebarea «Vii?» înaintea alergărilor`), because every list of topics wraps each name in a pair of quotes of its own.

**The notice is the switch: `{{rsvpAsk}}` (§562, §613, §754, §758's pattern), and the consent is the subscriber's own, given under it.** The question is queued and sent only to a subscriber whose `privacy_notice_version` is at or above `findFirstRsvpAskNoticeVersion` (the §421 line, as for the names on a list); the manage page records the version in force when the topic, or everything, is newly ticked, the server refuses the topic from the pop-up and from the manage page while the notice is silent on it, and unticking it deletes the question's unanswered rows. The question writes a «Vin!» row from a subscriber's address and mails them automatically; neither the newsletter's paragraph nor «Vin!»'s said so. The privacy notice's template gets the marker `{{rsvpAsk}}` — the topic's own name, quoted — in the two paragraphs of section 5 that describe it (the newsletter's: the automatic question the day before; «Vin!»'s: the address is written as an unconfirmed answer when the question is sent, and deleted at «Nu vin» or after 7 days). `{{newsletterTopics}}` leaves the topic out (it lists what a subscriber chooses and the club writes about; `AUTOMATIC_TOPICS` aside), so the notice names the topic through `{{rsvpAsk}}` alone and a notice approved before names nothing of it. The question is queued (`queueRsvpAsks`), sent (`prepareRsvpAsk`) and offered (the pop-up through `cachedRsvpAskDescribed`, the subscriber's page through `noticeDescribesRsvpAsk`, kept visible there for someone who ticked it already) only while the notice in force names `{{rsvpAsk}}` **and** `{{rsvp}}` in every language. `/admin/tasks` carries the row `rsvpAskNotice` while an upcoming event is ticked and the notice is silent; approving any legal text wakes the maintenance job, so a window already open is not slept through. A lawyer reads both paragraphs first.

**When, once (amends §775).** `queueRsvpAsks(db, now)` is a step of the maintenance job beside `queueNewEventAlerts`. It asks an event on the club's calendar day BEFORE the day its start falls on (Europe/Bucharest — never «24 hours before», which is the wrong day twice a year; the 08:00 hour sits between the two changes of the clock and midnight is never inside one, so both are found on the wall clock with `fromWallTimeInput`), at the first run at or after **08:00 club time** (the morning of §775's digest: nothing at 03:00) and until the midnight that opens the event's day. So an event at 10:00 on Sunday is asked on Saturday from 08:00; one at 00:30 on Sunday is asked on Saturday from 08:00 too; **one ticked only on the day itself is never asked** (its window closed at midnight, and a question about «tomorrow» on the day would be a lie — the page's «Vin!» still takes the answer); one ticked at 22:00 the evening before is asked at the first run after the save. The event's row in `event_rsvp_asks` — UNIQUE on the event — is the «once», written in the same transaction as the messages; an event with nobody to ask still gets its row (a subscriber who joins tomorrow is not asked about today's event). A cancelled, unticked, registering, draft, undated or members-only event (§552) is never asked and gets no row; a cancelled event's row, once written, stays, so it is not asked a second time if put back the same day. Whoever already has a **confirmed** answer to the event (compared on the canonical address, AGENTS.md §10.4) is not asked. Because the job sleeps when nothing is due (§334), `nextMaintenanceWork` now includes each such event's window opening, or the job would sleep through the morning. **At the send the window is checked again** (`rsvpAskDue`): a send held past midnight (a failure, the hourly pace) or an event moved out of «tomorrow» is withdrawn, not mailed as «mâine»; a moved event is not asked again for its new day (the queue is once per event, and the per-subscriber idempotency keys would have to carry the day). The retention sweep deletes the row with the event's other rows, thirty days after its end (and not at a cancellation, for the reason above); it holds an event id and a count, nothing personal.

**The two links are §812's, not a new kind.** The message is queued with the subscriber's id and the event's, nothing secret. When it is **sent** (`prepareRsvpAsk`, called by the renderer, AGENTS.md §14.5) the subscriber's «Vin!» row for the event is made — unconfirmed, no name, no tick, `asked_at` set — and the existing `RSVP_CONFIRM` and `RSVP_WITHDRAW` links are minted for it by `mintRsvpLinks`; only their SHA-256 is kept, they work once, «Vin» for 48 hours (never past the start), «Nu vin» until the start. Both buttons open the token page of §812 (`/vin/<link>`, `/en/coming/<link>`) whose GET changes nothing (BR-REQ-036-02 criterion 4: a mail scanner opens every link first); the press is a POST. «Vin» is `confirmRsvp` — the personal link is the proof of the address, so it is a verified press: counted at once, no second email, the browser remembered for a year as for any press of a link (it calls `confirmRsvp` with the token's own proof; the `link` source of `identity.ts` stays free for a later surface). The email says what happens: «Vin», then «Da, vin» on the page that opens — a GET never counts. «Nu vin» is `withdrawRsvp` on the same row: it is deleted, the person is simply not on the list, and the page says «Bine, nu te numărăm. Poți răspunde altfel până la start.» **It remembers no browser**: the person declined a question they never started, and the notice justifies the cookies as strictly necessary to a function the person asked for (`withdrawRsvp` reports `unanswered`, read from the deleted row; the page's sentence is carried by a keyed proof that includes it, so a typed `?nu=1` changes nothing). **What was extended in the §812 rules:** `rsvp.ts` gains the filter `ASKED_UNANSWERED` (`asked_at` set, never confirmed), which `requestWithdrawLink`, `listRsvpsForAdmin` and `countRsvpsForAdmin` apply; `answerRsvp` clears `asked_at` when the address is typed on the page; `withdrawRsvp` and `RsvpProved` gain `unanswered`; `confirmRsvp` takes the optional name and the tick, applied only to a row the email made (`asked_at`), still unconfirmed and still nameless, so a name typed by someone on the page is never replaced and a counted row is never renamed; the link read (`readRsvpLink`) says whether the answer was asked and named; the page of the links shows, for an asked row only, the same box «Numele tău (opțional)» and the tick «Vreau să apar cu numele» as the event page's card above the one button, with the link to the privacy notice, and the asked-specific words for «Nu vin». The newsletter's row has no name, so a one-tap «Vin» counts the person with no name and no tick — a name nobody typed is never made up.

**Taking over an unconfirmed row.** If the address was typed on the page and its own «Da, vin» link is still LIVE, the question is withdrawn and the page's answer is left as it is (that email is already a one-tap path, and minting here would supersede its link). If that link was never sent, spent or superseded, the ask takes the row over: the name and the tick on it were typed by whoever typed the address (§812: an unconfirmed row never lends a stranger's name to a verified press), so they are cleared and the row's age restarts, so the seven days of an unanswered row count from this email. The reverse (the page's message sent after the question) still supersedes the question's links and leaves the person that message. A message whose reason is gone by the time it is sent — the subscriber unsubscribed, unticked the topic or consented under a notice that did not name the question, the address already counted, the event cancelled, unticked, given a registration, made the members', started, or the notice no longer naming «Vin!» or the question, or the window closed — is withdrawn (`OutboxMessageWithdrawn`), not failed (§331).

**The road.** The message type `RSVP_ASK` (audience public, rendered by the newsletter's renderer so it carries the newsletter's manage link and privacy line) leaves by the **newsletter's** group (Mailgun) and its **bulk road** (`BULK_MESSAGE_TYPES`), as the new-event alert does: one message per subscriber of a topic is exactly the burst that must not spend the share kept for registrations' links, nor spill to the club's Gmail when Mailgun throttles. A question still held when its window closes is withdrawn at the send (above), so waiting last in line costs a question, never a wrong word. Unsubscribing deletes the subscriber's pending question and the unanswered «Vin!» row it made, on the spot. No club copy is queued for it (an automatic question, not a message about a person), and `/admin/emails` carries a card for it whose «când» line reads the hour from the one constant (`RSVP_ASK_CLOCK`).

**Open for the owner and the lawyer.** (1) The notice's newsletter paragraph and `{{newsletterTopics}}`: a notice approved before the topic existed does not name it; a lawyer reads the paragraph when it is approved again. (2) A subscriber to «Toate noutățile» who chose it under a notice that names the question (or any who ticked the topic) gets this question for every ticked event — one email per event, so two ticked events on the same day are two emails; the club decides how often to tick weekly runs. (3) A moved event is not asked again for its new day. (4) An unanswered question (`asked_at` set, no `confirmed_at`) is **not an answer**: the editor's fold and counts leave it out (the Organizer never sees it; an Administrator sees it in «Toate datele unei persoane» alone), and «Nu mai vin» on the page finds nothing in it (no withdraw link is mailed for an address nobody typed); «Toate datele unei persoane» keeps the row, labelled «întrebat …, fără răspuns». An address typed on the page afterwards makes the row the page's own again (`asked_at` cleared). (5) `/admin/emails`' list of what will be sent does not forecast the question yet. (6) Existing subscribers to «Toate noutățile» are not asked until they choose again on their page (it records the version in force when the topic, or everything, is newly ticked): the club may prefer to mail them once, which is its decision and a lawyer's.

**Refused.** A new token table or a new link purpose (the existing two are exactly «Vin» and «Nu vin»); counting a typed or guessed address (the link is minted for a confirmed subscriber's own address, at the send); sending the question through the announcements' group; reusing «Alergările săptămânale» (it promised once per series); asking on the day itself; asking someone already counted; a composer choice for the topic; and a club copy of every ask.
changelogLine: - **«Vii mâine la …?» by email** — the day before a ticked run, from 08:00 club time, the newsletter's subscribers of the new topic «Întrebarea «Vii?» înaintea alergărilor» get one email with **«Vin»** (counted at once, with an optional name) and **«Nu vin»** (counted nowhere), once per event. §NNN.

specsCriteria.text: Given the «Vii mâine la …?» email (`RSVP_ASK`), when it is queued, then its payload names only the subscriber and the event; when it is sent, then its two links are minted for the subscriber's own «Vin!» row (`RSVP_CONFIRM` and `RSVP_WITHDRAW`), only their hashes are stored, a newer message's links supersede them, no link carries the address, a GET of either changes nothing, «Vin» counts the subscriber on the press and «Nu vin» deletes the row so nobody is counted, «Nu vin» remembers no browser, and a message whose event, subscriber (still on the topic, and consenting under a notice that names it), notice (naming `{{rsvpAsk}}` as well as `{{rsvp}}`) or window of «tomorrow» no longer allows it is withdrawn rather than sent, while an unanswered question is not counted as an answer anywhere (2026-10-18, `DECISIONS.md` §NNN).

batchLine: the day before a ticked run, the newsletter's subscribers are asked «Vii?» with one-tap «Vin» / «Nu vin» links
